_design_notes: Scale-Factor break-even sweep — spark vs spark-openivm.
Goal: identify the SF at which spark-openivm starts to outperform vanilla
spark, both in aggregate (batch totals) AND per dbt model.
Per-experiment lifecycle (executed serially by the OAT runner):
1. Disk pre-flight (>=OAT_MIN_FREE_PCT, default 10% free) — if not, skip.
2. Datagen for THIS SF (idempotent — usually fresh because the previous
iteration's cleanup wiped mount/raw/<SF>/).
3. Engine bench (spark, spark-openivm) — serial, NOT parallel, so each
engine gets the full host budget.
4. Result persistence to mount/results/<SF>/dbt-server/ AND oat_experiments.
5. Cleanup: wipe mount/raw/<SF>/, mount/results/<SF>/{spark,spark-openivm}/,
mount/logs/<SF>/{spark,spark-openivm}/. Keep dbt-server/, stats/, bin/,
benchmark-state/ so charts and history survive.
SF list is non-uniform on purpose: smaller granularity at small SFs (where
openivm overhead dominates) and larger steps at the tail (where the raw
data volume changes the question from 'who wins' to 'do we still fit on
disk'). The sweep stops gracefully if disk drops below 10% — the harness
still emits the chart with whatever experiments completed.
Knobs that ARE swept (one-at-a-time, knob = scale_factor):
Knobs held at baseline:
batch_1_pct = 100   (full historical batch)
batch_2_pct = 1     (1% incremental delta)
batch_3_pct = 2     (2% incremental delta)
engines     = [spark, spark-openivm]
parallel    = false (serial; full host per engine)
feature_flags.openivm_validate        = true
feature_flags.openivm_profile_refresh = true
feature_flags.openivm_query_log       = true
feature_flags.preserve_raw            = false  (no-op inside OAT)
spark_tunables.*                      = inherit YAML
Disk sizing:
~170 MB raw per unit SF; ~6x including delta + per-engine outputs.
At SF=1000, raw alone is ~170 GB. We expect the disk-guard to trip
somewhere between SF=400 and SF=1000 on a host with <1 TB free.
